newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-SBC first half profit jumps 84 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-SBC first half profit jumps 84 pct.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) on Wednesday said 1997 first half net profit rose 84 percent, the strongest rise reported by Switzerland's Big Three Banks.

SBC also said in its half-year report that it would "comfortably exceed" a 1997 net profit target of 1.7 billion Swiss francs ($1.1 billion) despite an expected decline in results in the second half from a strong first half.
The forecast was more confident than earlier statements by Switzerland's third-biggest bank. Previously SBC had only said it was confident of achieving its 1997 profit goal.
SBC said all its four divisions contributed to the excellent result and earnings from investment banking unit SBC Warburg for the first time made up the largest share of group profits.
The profit rise was well-above analysts' forecasts, but SBC's share was lower in pre-bourse trading, quoted at 416/417 francs, down 0.5 francs.
Analysts had expected SBC to report a first-half profit rise of between 50 and 70 percent.
"This is significantly better than expected," said Hans Kaufmann, senior analyst at Bank Julius Baer, noting that he would be revising upwards his full-year earnings forecast.

SBC's group net profit in the first half rose 84 percent to 1.326 billion francs ($868.8 million), reflecting "the bank's substantially stronger earnings capability in a favourable financial market environment," SBC said in a statement.
Efforts to improve the profitability of SBC's personal and commercial banking in Switzerland -- for years the problem child of all Swiss banks -- had the desired effect, SBC said.
First half net profit at SBC Switzerland soared 750 percent to 119 million francs from 14 million.
Profits at SBC Warburg soared 60 percent to 691 million, surpassing profits from SBC's Private Banking division, which rose 36 percent to 653 million.
SBC Brinson, which manages institutional assets, rose 121.4 percent to 62 million, partially because income from managing mutual funds taken over from SBC Private Banking.
Exuberant stock markets helped SBC' trading income rise 43 percent to 2.233 billion francs with most of the growth coming from client-related business.

But fee and commission income remains the cornerstone of SBC, rising 29 percent to 2.719 billion francs. The strongest growth came in securities handling commissions, follwed by asset management fees.
"This growth was driven by healthy financial market activity and higher assets under management," SBC said.
SBC's loan-loss provisions in the first half were 98 million francs higher than a budgeted level of 325 million, which was based on a new risk accounting system.
SBC also took an additional 160 million francs from first-half income as ordinary provisions to cover continued weakness in the Swsis real estate market.

SBC adopted a new system last year for statistically forecasting credit risk, called Actuarial Credit Risk Accounting (ACRA), as part of a wider effort by Swiss banks to settle a mounting backlog of bad domestic loans.
In connection with ACRA, SBC took a one-time charge of 2.080 billion in 1996 to absorb risks above the projected mean.
SBC's statement said the statistically expected credit provisions for 1997 totalled 650 million, half of which were charged to the first six months.
"Actual provisioning needs for the first half, however, were 423 million Swiss francs," SBC said.
-- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340 ($ = 1.526 Swiss Francs)
